title: Content of photographs – what is being depicted?

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines
location.section: Content of photographs – what is being depicted?

slide_intent: Choose photographic subjects that reveal a particular city and its people because familiar clichés can conceal what makes a place distinctive.
strategic_value: Inclusive subjects, nearby nature and everyday resilience can make Helsinki’s stated character concrete.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section compares captioned photo pairs covering freedom, urban nature, extraordinary conditions and a functional city, with crosses marking less suitable examples in the illustrated context.
practical_value: Select subjects for the story they tell about Helsinki and assess context rather than treating a crossed example as universally forbidden.

content_islands.name: Selection premise
content_islands.spec: Explain freedom, equality and the contextual meaning of crossed examples.

content_islands.name: People and nature pairs
content_islands.spec: Compare diverse activity scenes and urban/natural connections.

content_islands.name: Atmosphere pairs
content_islands.spec: Contrast distinctive light, weather and city character with generic scenes.

content_islands.name: Functionality pairs
content_islands.spec: Finish with events and everyday operation in challenging conditions.

ingredient.name: Photographic subject selection
ingredient.role: Make city values tangible through recognizable situations.
ingredient.application: Choose diverse people, distinctive Helsinki settings and stories linking urban life with nature or functionality.
ingredient.scope: Crossed photographs are contextual comparisons; the source explicitly says they could work in the right context.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text connects photographs to freedom, equality, wildly urban character and sustainable functionality.
reference_purposes.Application: Captioned comparisons explain why particular subjects tell a stronger Helsinki story.
